observed.facings.png: A single south panel at shared scale. A low barrier runs diagonally from upper left to lower right. It has dark brown horizontal timber boards between four square timber posts, with the last two posts close together at the right end. Each post has grey metal collars with bolts at top and base and a flat grey pyramidal cap. Vertical grey bolted bracket strips hold the board ends. A brown lumpy mud bank lies along the front foot, with small wet dark rings where the posts enter the ground. The background is transparent checkerboard. There is no red paint and no yellow/black tape.
observed.south.png: The same picture at native panel size. Dark stained boards with some green-black grime along the lowest board, light grey brackets and caps, and a mud strip at the base. The cut-out is clean, with no halo or backdrop visible.
observed.scale.png: The barrier sits on a flat brown ground beside a vanilla human. It is about as wide as the human is tall and reaches roughly the human's waist to chest. No footprint outline is visible in this panel.
observed.siblings.png: Reference row of Scrapper (rusty timber with patch plates and rope), Industrial (grey cast concrete with stains) and Futuristic (white panels with cyan light strips). All share the same layout, post arrangement, mud bank and camera as the candidate.

The south sprite shows visible upper surfaces on the post caps and board edges, with upright posts and parallel receding edges. Seeing two vertical faces of a square post is compatible with the specified orthographic camera; the diagonal barrier alignment does not demonstrate a camera error.

In south.png, an irregular brown strip containing soil clods and stones extends along the entire barrier and beyond both ends. Dark wet-looking rings surround the post feet. These features also remain visible in the scale and assembled panels.

request.subject: RM_SiltTrap_Modern

edits.change: The sprite is the barrier alone, cut out cleanly: pressure-treated dark timber boards, square posts and galvanized steel brackets and caps stand on a fully transparent background, with transparent alpha between and around the post feet and below the bottom edge.

Each post foot ends in a crisp, clean-cut base with a dark outline, and the lowest board edge is a straight outlined line. Silt appears only as a thin, tight sliver of damp sediment pressed against the upstream face of the boards, its edge hugging the timber so it reads as part of the structure.
The ground plane is absent: the silt-trap barrier floats as an isolated object on transparency, as a vanilla RimWorld building sprite does, with no mud patch, stones or wet rings beneath it.

invariants: Modern look: pressure-treated dark timber boards and square posts with galvanized steel brackets and caps, a plain structure of today
Natural galvanized grey steel and dark brown timber only, with no hazard stripes and no tier-marker paint colour
Riverbank silt barrier with no ports and nothing to connect, Graphic_Single, square 1.2 x 1.2 framing
Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline
Top-down three-quarter building view matching the other looks' scale beside a human
request.prompt: A single RimWorld building sprite: a modern riverbank silt-trap baffle barrier. Pressure-treated dark brown timber boards stacked horizontally between square timber posts, fastened with galvanized steel brackets and steel post caps, a plain practical structure of today in natural galvanized grey and dark timber tones with no hazard stripes and no painted tier colour. A thin, tight sliver of damp silt sits pressed against the boards, its edge hugging the timber so it reads as part of the structure. The barrier is cut out cleanly on a fully transparent background: each post foot ends in a crisp clean-cut base with a dark outline, the lowest board edge is a straight outlined line, and transparent alpha shows between and around the post feet, with the barrier standing alone as an isolated object and nothing beneath it. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, square framing for a 1.2 x 1.2 Graphic_Single. Keep the palette, timber and steel construction and proportions from the previous render.

subject: RM_SiltTrap_Industrial

reply.subject: RM_SiltTrap_Industrial

observed.facings.png: A single south panel on a checker background. A raw grey concrete barrier runs diagonally from upper left to lower right, seen obliquely from above. Four square posts with chamfered, lit tops frame two recessed cast panels, and the last two posts stand close together at the right end. The surface shows board-form lines, a horizontal pour seam, tie holes weeping rust, spalled patches, a small bent rusty rebar stub on the top of the second panel, and dark green-black algae staining along the bottom. A brown mud bank with clods lies along the front, and thin water rings surround the post feet on the right.
observed.south.png: The same picture alone at its native size. The cut-out is clean on the checker. Grey stained concrete reads clearly, with lit post tops, grime at the base, a mud strip and small water edges at the post feet. No backdrop or halo is visible.
observed.scale.png: The barrier on a brown ground beside a vanilla human. The barrier stands about two thirds of the human's height and is about as long as one to two pawn widths. It reads as a low cement fence with four posts. The mud base merges slightly with the ground colour.
observed.siblings.png: Reference panels for the other three looks. Scrapper is rusty planks with rope-lashed posts, Modern is dark timber planks with grey steel brackets and caps, and Futuristic is white panels with cyan light strips. All three share the same diagonal run, post rhythm, doubled end post, mud bank and water line.
observed.assembled_1.png: An offline row of Scrapper, Industrial, Modern and Futuristic beside a human. Industrial has the same silhouette, size and placement as the others. It is the palest and least colourful after Futuristic, and it reads as plain concrete. Posts draw in front of the panels and the mud sits below them.
observed.assembled_2.png: A smaller game-scale row. The Industrial barrier still reads as a pale grey four-post wall on a dark base and stays distinct from the rust-orange, dark-brown and white-cyan looks. Surface detail has mostly merged into a mottled grey. The overlapping labels come from the panel layout, not the art.
observed.assembled_3.png: The smallest row, near 32 px per cell. The Industrial barrier is a small pale grey fence with posts still separable and a dark foot. The stains and tie holes are gone, but the silhouette and the grey material identity hold. The overlapping labels come from the panel layout, not the art.

CAMERA.seen: It uses the same oblique camera as the siblings: lit parallelogram post tops and panel coping are visible, with front faces below. It is not a side elevation.

LAYERS.seen: Posts overlap the panels behind them, the nearer end post overlaps the one behind it, and the mud bank and water rings sit at the feet. The offline rows show no ordering errors. No attached parts exist because this look has no ports.

ROTATIONS.seen: It is Graphic_Single with one south picture, so the same picture is used on every rotation. No facing can disagree in parts or palette.

SIGNATURE.seen: It reads as a riverbank silt barrier: a cast baffle wall with posts, a mud bank along the front and water at the feet. It keeps the sibling silhouette, canvas, mud base and water line, and it looks raw, stained, utilitarian and not colourful, as described.

MATERIAL.seen: The grey reads as cast cement, with form-board lines, a pour seam, tie holes with rust weeps, spalling and algae staining at the waterline. It does not read as a coat of paint.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The whole barrier sits inside the canvas with margin, measures 190 px of visible height, and matches the siblings' extent and placement. It neither overflows nor floats.

ALPHA.seen: The cut-out is clean with real alpha and no backdrop or halo. The only ground elements are the mud base and water line, which the description requires and the siblings share.

OURS.seen: It is the same custom silhouette as the family, redrawn in concrete. Nothing in it reads as vanilla or another mod's art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: It is an ugly cement-looking barrier, grey and stained, with no bright red and no yellow/black tape. The Modern sibling on the panel is not this subject.

LEGIBLE.seen: In the smallest assembled row it is still a pale grey four-post wall with a dark foot, and it stays distinct from the other three looks, though fine stains are lost.

findings.seen: At the smallest scale the staining, tie holes and spalls merge into flat pale grey, so the 'ugly, stained' character mostly disappears. The silhouette still reads.
findings.quote: Textures are authored at about 128 px per cell; the player sees 32 px per cell in normal play and up to 128–256 px per cell zoomed in. Both must work.
findings.fix: The concrete carries a few larger, darker water-stain streaks and a stronger dark band at the base, so the grime still shows at 32 px per cell.

proposals: The small bent rebar stub on the second panel's top is thin and slightly twig-like at normal zoom. A straighter, shorter rusty stub, or a pair of them, would read more clearly as exposed reinforcement.
